text: 红雨随心翻作浪，青山着意化为桥
pinyin: hóng yǔ suí xīn fān zuò làng, qīng shān zhuó yì huà wéi qiáo
literal: red · rain · follow · heart · turn · into · waves, green · hills · with · intent · become · bridges
natural: at will the red rain turns to waves, and the green hills are made into bridges

meaning.en: Mao Zedong's couplet imagining a people who bend nature to their will: the 'red rain' of fallen blossoms becomes waves and the mountains become bridges.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东的诗句，想象人民意志坚定、改造自然：落花如红雨随心化作波浪，青山有意变成通途。

equivalents: move mountains and tame the waves
bend nature to our will

examples.zh: 他在讲话里引用“红雨随心翻作浪，青山着意化为桥”，鼓励大家改造山河。
examples.en: In his speech he quoted 'the red rain turns to waves at will, the green hills become bridges', urging everyone to remake the land.

examples.zh: 这副对联用的是“红雨随心翻作浪，青山着意化为桥”，气势很足。
examples.en: The couplet uses 'the red rain turns to waves at will, the green hills become bridges', and has real sweep.

origin.source: 毛泽东《七律二首·送瘟神》

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote the two-part poem 'Farewell to the God of Plague' in July 1958; this couplet comes from the second poem.
story.zh: 毛泽东1958年7月作《七律二首·送瘟神》，此联出自第二首。

usage.en: Quoted for confident, transformative ambition. Written in 1958 in response to the news that schistosomiasis had been eliminated in Yujiang County; the line is usually quoted for its imagery rather than its occasion. 着意 is read zhuó yì here.
usage.zh: 常用来形容改造自然、改天换地的豪情。此诗作于1958年，因闻余江县消灭血吸虫病而作；今天多取其意象来引用。“着意”读 zhuó yì。

text: 不管风吹浪打，胜似闲庭信步
pinyin: bù guǎn fēng chuī làng dǎ, shèng sì xián tíng xìn bù
literal: no matter · wind · blow · waves · beat, better · than · idle · courtyard · stroll
natural: whatever the wind and waves, it beats a stroll around the courtyard

meaning.en: Mao Zedong's line on facing storms with ease: however hard the wind blows and the waves beat, it feels better than a leisurely walk in a courtyard.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东的诗句：不管风吹浪打，面对它们比在庭院里悠闲散步还要畅快，形容临危不惧、从容自若。

equivalents: unfazed by the storm
take the rough with a smile

examples.zh: 面对质疑，她镇定自若，真是“不管风吹浪打，胜似闲庭信步”。
examples.en: Facing the doubters she stayed calm: truly 'no matter the wind and waves, better than a stroll in the courtyard'.

examples.zh: 船在大浪里颠簸，老船长却“不管风吹浪打，胜似闲庭信步”。
examples.en: The ship pitched in heavy seas, yet the old captain was, in the poem's words, 'unmoved by wind and waves, as if strolling in a courtyard'.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Prelude to Water Melody: Swimming' in June 1956 after swimming across the Yangtze at Wuhan.
story.zh: 毛泽东1956年6月畅游长江后作《水调歌头·游泳》。

usage.en: Quoted to praise calm courage under pressure. The poem was written in 1956 after Mao swam in the Yangtze at Wuhan. The second half, 胜似闲庭信步, is often used alone.
usage.zh: 常用来称赞压力下的从容和勇气。此词作于1956年毛泽东畅游长江之后。后半句“胜似闲庭信步”也常单独使用。

text: 萧瑟秋风今又是，换了人间
pinyin: xiāo sè qiū fēng jīn yòu shì, huàn le rén jiān
literal: desolate · autumn · wind · today · again · is, changed · the · human · world
natural: the desolate autumn wind blows again today, but the world of men has changed

meaning.en: Mao Zedong's line: the same bleak autumn wind blows as in Cao Cao's day, but the human world has been transformed.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东的诗句：秋风依旧萧瑟，如同当年曹操所见，但人间已经换了新貌。

equivalents: the wind is the same, the world is not
everything has changed except the autumn wind

examples.zh: 重回故地，他想起“萧瑟秋风今又是，换了人间”，感慨万千。
examples.en: Back at the old place, he thought of 'the autumn wind blows again, yet the world has changed' and was deeply moved.

examples.zh: 作文的结尾引了“萧瑟秋风今又是，换了人间”，对比今昔。
examples.en: The essay closed with 'the desolate autumn wind blows again, yet the world has changed', contrasting past and present.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote 'Waves Washing the Sand: Beidaihe' in 1954, echoing Cao Cao's 'Looking at the Sea' with its image of the autumn wind.
story.zh: 毛泽东1954年作《浪淘沙·北戴河》，与曹操《观沧海》遥相呼应，写到萧瑟秋风。

usage.en: Quoted when contrasting an unchanged scene with a changed world. The poem answers Cao Cao's 《观沧海》 and was written in 1954 at Beidaihe; the line is mostly quoted for the contrast between enduring nature and changing society.
usage.zh: 用于对比景物依旧而世事全非。此词作于1954年北戴河，呼应曹操《观沧海》；多取自然依旧、人间已变的对比。

text: 占人类总数四分之一的中国人从此站立起来了
pinyin: zhàn rén lèi zǒng shù sì fēn zhī yī de zhōng guó rén cóng cǐ zhàn lì qǐ lái le
literal: occupy · humanity · total · one-quarter · 's · Chinese · people · from · now · stand · up · [done]
natural: the Chinese, a quarter of humanity, have from now on stood up

meaning.en: Mao Zedong's declaration at the founding of the People's Republic: the Chinese people, a quarter of mankind, have risen to their feet.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东在新中国成立前夕的宣告：占世界人口四分之一的中国人民从此站立起来了。

equivalents: the Chinese people have stood up
a quarter of humanity has risen

examples.zh: 纪念馆里展示着“占人类总数四分之一的中国人从此站立起来了”的手稿。
examples.en: The museum displays the manuscript of 'the Chinese, a quarter of humanity, have from now on stood up'.

examples.zh: 历史课上，老师讲到占人类总数四分之一的中国人从此站立起来了这句话。
examples.en: In history class the teacher discussed the line 'the Chinese, a quarter of humanity, have from now on stood up'.

origin.source: 毛泽东《中国人民站起来了》（1949年）

story.en: Mao Zedong delivered the opening address at the first plenary session of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference on 21 September 1949, shortly before the founding of the People's Republic.
story.zh: 1949年9月21日，毛泽东在中国人民政治协商会议第一届全体会议上致开幕词，不久后新中国成立。

usage.en: A historical quotation, usually cited in connection with 1949. The full sentence in the speech is longer; this part is the usual quoted form. The familiar short form 中国人民站起来了 is the speech's title.
usage.zh: 历史性引语，多与1949年联系在一起。原文后接“……我们的民族将从此列入爱好和平自由的世界各民族的大家庭”，此处为常引部分。常见短语“中国人民站起来了”是该讲话的题目。

text: 谁是我们的敌人？谁是我们的朋友？这个问题是革命的首要问题
pinyin: shéi shì wǒ men de dí rén, shéi shì wǒ men de péng you, zhè gè wèn tí shì gé mìng de shǒu yào wèn tí
literal: who · is · our · enemy, who · is · our · friend, this · question · is · revolution · 's · primary · question
natural: who are our enemies? who are our friends? this is the first question of revolution

meaning.en: The opening lines of Mao Zedong's 1925 essay: telling enemies from friends is the first question any revolution must settle.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东1925年文章的开头：分清敌友，是革命首先要解决的问题。

equivalents: know friend from foe
first, work out who is on your side

examples.zh: 现代政治课常提到“谁是我们的敌人？谁是我们的朋友？这个问题是革命的首要问题”。
examples.en: Modern politics classes often cite 'who are our enemies? who are our friends? this is the first question of revolution'.

examples.zh: 他在分析形势时套用了“谁是我们的敌人？谁是我们的朋友？这个问题是革命的首要问题”这句话。
examples.en: In assessing the situation he borrowed the line 'who are our enemies? who are our friends? this is the first question of revolution'.

origin.source: 毛泽东《中国社会各阶级的分析》

story.en: Mao Zedong's 1925 essay 'Analysis of the Classes in Chinese Society' opens with these sentences.
story.zh: 毛泽东1925年的文章《中国社会各阶级的分析》开篇即是这几句话。

usage.en: Quoted when someone stresses the need to identify opponents and allies first; sometimes used loosely outside politics. The essay dates from 1925.
usage.zh: 在强调首先要分清对手和盟友时引用，有时也泛用于政治之外。此文作于1925年。

text: 世界上怕就怕认真二字，共产党就最讲认真
pinyin: shì jiè shàng pà jiù pà rèn zhēn èr zì, gòng chǎn dǎng jiù zuì jiǎng rèn zhēn
literal: world · on · fear · just · fear · earnest · two · characters, Communist · Party · just · most · stress · earnest
natural: what the world fears most is the word 'earnest', and the Communist Party values earnestness above all

meaning.en: A saying widely attributed to Mao Zedong: nothing is hard if you take it seriously, and the Party prizes being earnest above all.
meaning.zh: 相传为毛泽东所说：世上无难事，只怕认真，而共产党最讲认真。

equivalents: nothing is impossible to the earnest
anything can be done if you take it seriously

examples.zh: 他把“世界上怕就怕认真二字，共产党就最讲认真”写在办公桌前。
examples.en: He put 'the world fears only earnestness, and the Party prizes earnestness most' on the wall in front of his desk.

examples.zh: 开会时领导强调：世界上怕就怕认真二字，共产党就最讲认真。
examples.en: At the meeting the leader stressed: 'the world fears only earnestness, and the Party prizes earnestness most'.

usage.en: Widely attributed to Mao Zedong, but the exact occasion and date are not reliably documented, so it is given here without a source. Usually quoted in the workplace or in official speeches to urge conscientiousness; the saying 世上无难事，只怕有心人 is a close relative.
usage.zh: 相传为毛泽东所说，但具体场合和年代并无可靠出处，故不标出处。多在工作场合或官方讲话中用来强调认真负责。与“世上无难事，只怕有心人”意思相近。

text: 下定决心，不怕牺牲，排除万难，去争取胜利
pinyin: xià dìng jué xīn, bù pà xī shēng, pái chú wàn nán, qù zhēng qǔ shèng lì
literal: make · up · mind, not · fear · sacrifice, remove · ten-thousand · difficulties, go · strive · for · victory
natural: make up your mind, fear no sacrifice, sweep away every difficulty, and go for victory

meaning.en: Mao Zedong's call to resolve, sacrifice and perseverance: decide firmly, shrink from no sacrifice, overcome every obstacle and win.
meaning.zh: 毛泽东的号召：下定决心，不惧牺牲，克服一切困难，去夺取胜利。

equivalents: be resolute and fear no sacrifice
overcome all obstacles to win

examples.zh: 动员会上，他喊出了“下定决心，不怕牺牲，排除万难，去争取胜利”。
examples.en: At the rally he called out 'make up your mind, fear no sacrifice, sweep away every difficulty, and go for victory'.

examples.zh: 球队更衣室的墙上写着：下定决心，不怕牺牲，排除万难，去争取胜利。
examples.en: On the changing-room wall was written: 'make up your mind, fear no sacrifice, sweep away every difficulty, and go for victory'.

story.en: In 'The Foolish Old Man Who Removed the Mountains' (the closing speech of the Seventh National Congress of the Communist Party, June 1945), Mao used the old fable to urge perseverance; this sentence comes from that text.
story.zh: 毛泽东在《愚公移山》（1945年6月中共七大闭幕词）中借用愚公移山的寓言号召坚持不懈，这句话出自该文。

usage.en: Typically used in rallying speeches and slogans. 排除万难 is also a chengyu in its own right.
usage.zh: 多用于动员讲话和口号。“排除万难”本身也是成语。

text: 面壁十年图破壁，难酬蹈海亦英雄
pinyin: miàn bì shí nián tú pò bì, nán chóu dǎo hǎi yì yīng xióng
literal: face · wall · ten · years · aim · break · wall, hard · to · fulfil · leap · into · sea · still · hero
natural: ten years facing the wall to break through it; if the aim fails, leaping into the sea is still heroic

meaning.en: Zhou Enlai's youthful couplet: devote ten years, like a meditating monk, to breaking through the wall; even if the goal is out of reach, to die for it is heroic.
meaning.zh: 周恩来青年时代的诗句：像达摩面壁一样潜心十年，志在破壁；即使壮志难酬，蹈海而死也不失英雄本色。

equivalents: ten years' toil to break through, with no regrets if it fails
to die trying is still heroic

examples.zh: 毕业赠言里，老师写下“面壁十年图破壁，难酬蹈海亦英雄”勉励学生。
examples.en: In the graduation message the teacher wrote 'ten years facing the wall to break through it' to encourage the students.

examples.zh: 他把“面壁十年图破壁，难酬蹈海亦英雄”抄在笔记本扉页。
examples.en: He copied 'ten years facing the wall to break through it; to fail at sea is still heroic' on the first page of his notebook.

origin.source: 周恩来《大江歌罢掉头东》（1917年）

story.en: Before leaving for Japan in 1917, Zhou Enlai wrote the poem 'Sing to the Great River and Head East' as a farewell present for a classmate.
story.zh: 1917年周恩来赴日留学前，作《大江歌罢掉头东》赠同窗好友。

usage.en: Quoted to express long, single-minded dedication to a goal. 面壁 alludes to Bodhidharma's nine years facing a wall; 蹈海 recalls Lu Zhonglian, who vowed to leap into the sea rather than serve Qin. Written by Zhou Enlai, aged about 19, as a farewell to a classmate before he went to study in Japan in 1917.
usage.zh: 用来表达多年专心致志、不怕失败的决心。“面壁”借用达摩面壁九年的典故，“蹈海”用鲁仲连义不帝秦、宁蹈东海的故事。1917年周恩来约十九岁，赴日留学前写此诗赠别同学。

text: 解放思想，实事求是，团结一致向前看
pinyin: jiě fàng sī xiǎng, shí shì qiú shì, tuán jié yī zhì xiàng qián kàn
literal: liberate · thinking, seek · truth · from · facts, unite · as · one · look · forward
natural: free the mind, seek truth from facts, unite and look ahead

meaning.en: Deng Xiaoping's 1978 formula for the start of reform: break free of rigid thinking, be guided by facts, and unite to look forward.
meaning.zh: 邓小平1978年提出的改革开放初期方针：摆脱僵化思想，从实际出发，团结一致，面向未来。

equivalents: free your mind and face the facts
leave dogma behind and look ahead

examples.zh: 会议开幕词提到“解放思想，实事求是，团结一致向前看”，定下了基调。
examples.en: The opening remarks mentioned 'free the mind, seek truth from facts, unite and look ahead', setting the tone.

examples.zh: 历史课本把“解放思想，实事求是，团结一致向前看”视为改革开放的起点。
examples.en: The history textbook treats 'free the mind, seek truth from facts, unite and look ahead' as the starting point of reform and opening up.

origin.source: 邓小平《解放思想，实事求是，团结一致向前看》（1978年）

story.en: Deng Xiaoping gave this speech on 13 December 1978 at the close of the Central Work Conference, which prepared the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee.
story.zh: 1978年12月13日，邓小平在中央工作会议闭幕会上发表此讲话，为十一届三中全会作准备。

usage.en: Mostly cited in historical or official contexts about the late-1970s turn to reform. 实事求是 is a chengyu in its own right and is also quoted separately.
usage.zh: 多见于谈论上世纪七十年代末改革开放转折的历史或官方文章。“实事求是”本身也是成语，常单独引用。

text: 冷静观察，稳住阵脚，沉着应对
pinyin: lěng jìng guān chá, wěn zhù zhèn jiǎo, chén zhuó yìng duì
literal: calmly · observe, steady · formation, composed · respond
natural: observe calmly, hold your ground, respond with composure

meaning.en: Deng Xiaoping's advice for a crisis: stay cool and watch, keep your position steady, and respond without panic.
meaning.zh: 邓小平对应对危机的建议：冷静地观察形势，稳住自己的阵地，沉着地应付。

equivalents: keep a cool head and hold steady
watch calmly, stand firm, react calmly

examples.zh: 股市大跌，他对客户说：冷静观察，稳住阵脚，沉着应对。
examples.en: When the market fell sharply he told his clients: 'observe calmly, hold your ground, respond with composure'.

examples.zh: 遇到突发状况，队长提醒大家“冷静观察，稳住阵脚，沉着应对”。
examples.en: Faced with a sudden crisis the captain reminded everyone: 'observe calmly, hold your ground, respond with composure'.

story.en: Deng Xiaoping gave this guidance in talks with senior colleagues in 1989 and 1990, in response to the international situation of those years.
story.zh: 1989至1990年间，邓小平针对当时的国际形势，在与中央负责同志的谈话中提出这一方针。

usage.en: Used outside politics as general advice to stay calm in a crisis. It comes from Deng Xiaoping's talks of 1989-1990 and is the first part of a longer set of guidelines (followed by 韬光养晦 and others).
usage.zh: 在政治之外也常作为危机中保持镇定的通用建议。出自邓小平1989至1990年间的谈话，是一组方针中的前半部分（后接“韬光养晦”等）。

pinyin: pín qióng bù shì shè huì zhǔ yì

meaning.en: Deng Xiaoping's slogan of the reform era: socialism should create wealth, and being poor is no proof of being socialist.
meaning.zh: 邓小平改革时期的名言：社会主义要消灭贫穷、发展生产力，贫穷并不是社会主义。

equivalents: being poor is not a virtue
socialism means getting rich together

examples.zh: 讲到改革的目的时，老师引用了“贫穷不是社会主义”。
examples.en: Speaking of the aim of reform, the teacher quoted 'poverty is not socialism'.

examples.zh: 展览的标语写着：贫穷不是社会主义。
examples.en: The exhibition slogan read: 'Poverty is not socialism'.

origin.source: 邓小平谈话（1980年代中期，另见1992年南方谈话）

story.en: Deng Xiaoping said this in his talks of the mid-1980s, and he repeated the idea in 1992.
story.zh: 邓小平在上世纪八十年代中期的谈话中说过这句话，1992年又重申此意。

usage.en: A historical and political quotation, cited when discussing reform and development. Deng said it, with small variations in wording, on several occasions from the mid-1980s to the 1992 southern tour.
usage.zh: 历史与政治引语，谈及改革与发展时引用。邓小平在上世纪八十年代中期到1992年南方谈话期间多次说过，措辞略有不同。

text: 教育要面向现代化，面向世界，面向未来
pinyin: jiào yù yào miàn xiàng xiàn dài huà, miàn xiàng shì jiè, miàn xiàng wèi lái
literal: education · must · face · modernisation, face · the world, face · the future
natural: education must face modernisation, face the world, face the future

meaning.en: Deng Xiaoping's three-part motto for education, written as an inscription for a Beijing school in 1983.
meaning.zh: 邓小平为教育事业题写的三面向题词，1983年题赠景山学校。

equivalents: education for modernisation, the world and the future
schooling that looks ahead

examples.zh: 许多学校把“教育要面向现代化，面向世界，面向未来”写在校园的墙上。
examples.en: Many schools put 'education must face modernisation, face the world, face the future' on their campus walls.

examples.zh: 会议上，校长重申教育要面向现代化，面向世界，面向未来。
examples.en: At the meeting the headmaster reaffirmed that education must face modernisation, face the world, face the future.

origin.source: 邓小平为景山学校题词（1983年）

story.en: In October 1983 Deng Xiaoping wrote this inscription for the Jingshan School in Beijing.
story.zh: 1983年10月，邓小平为北京景山学校题词。

usage.en: Often called the 'three orientations' (三个面向) and widely cited in education policy and school mottoes.
usage.zh: 常简称“三个面向”，在教育政策文件和学校校训中广泛引用。

text: 建设有中国特色的社会主义
pinyin: jiàn shè yǒu zhōng guó tè sè de shè huì zhǔ yì

meaning.en: Deng Xiaoping's formulation for the reform era: follow Chinese conditions and build socialism in a way that suits them.
meaning.zh: 邓小平提出的改革时期的提法：走自己的路，建设符合中国国情的社会主义。

equivalents: socialism with Chinese characteristics
a path suited to Chinese conditions

examples.zh: 报告的标题就是“建设有中国特色的社会主义”。
examples.en: The report was titled 'Build Socialism with Chinese Characteristics'.

examples.zh: 她研究的是改革开放以来建设有中国特色的社会主义的历程。
examples.en: She studies the course of building socialism with Chinese characteristics since reform and opening up.

origin.source: 邓小平在中共十二大开幕词（1982年）

story.en: Deng Xiaoping used the phrase in his opening speech to the 12th National Congress of the Communist Party on 1 September 1982.
story.zh: 1982年9月1日，邓小平在中共十二大开幕词中提出这一提法。

usage.en: A set political phrase, very common in official documents and textbooks.
usage.zh: 固定的政治提法，常见于官方文件和教科书。

text: 我是中国人民的儿子，我深情地爱着我的祖国和人民
pinyin: wǒ shì zhōng guó rén mín de ér zi, wǒ shēn qíng de ài zhe wǒ de zǔ guó hé rén mín
literal: I · am · Chinese · people · 's · son, I · deeply · lovingly · love · my · homeland · and · people
natural: I am a son of the Chinese people, and I love my country and my people deeply

meaning.en: A declaration attributed to Deng Xiaoping of his devotion to the country and its people.
meaning.zh: 据传为邓小平所说，表达对祖国和人民的深厚感情。

equivalents: a loyal son of the people
I love my country and its people dearly

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，他念出了“我是中国人民的儿子，我深情地爱着我的祖国和人民”。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony he read out 'I am a son of the Chinese people, and I love my country and my people deeply'.

examples.zh: 纪念展板上写着：我是中国人民的儿子，我深情地爱着我的祖国和人民。
examples.en: The memorial board read: 'I am a son of the Chinese people, and I love my country and my people deeply'.

usage.en: Widely quoted and attributed to Deng Xiaoping (early 1980s), but accounts differ on the exact occasion, so it is given here without a source. Used in patriotic or commemorative contexts.
usage.zh: 广为引用，通常认为是邓小平上世纪八十年代初所说，但具体场合说法不一，故不标出处。多用于爱国或纪念性的场合。

text: 大雪压青松，青松挺且直；要知松高洁，待到雪化时
pinyin: dà xuě yā qīng sōng, qīng sōng tǐng qiě zhí, yào zhī sōng gāo jié, dài dào xuě huà shí
literal: heavy · snow · presses · green · pine, green · pine · upright · and · straight, want · know · pine's · lofty · purity, wait · till · snow · melts · time
natural: heavy snow presses on the green pine, which stands tall and straight; to know its nobility, wait until the snow melts

meaning.en: Chen Yi's poem: the pine stays upright under heavy snow, and its noble character shows when the snow melts; a symbol of integrity under pressure.
meaning.zh: 陈毅的诗：青松在大雪重压下依然挺拔，等到雪化时才见它的高洁，比喻人在逆境中保持节操。

equivalents: true character shows under pressure
the pine stands tall under snow

examples.zh: 老师用“大雪压青松，青松挺且直；要知松高洁，待到雪化时”来鼓励受挫的学生。
examples.en: The teacher used 'heavy snow presses the pine, which stands tall and straight; to know its nobility, wait until the snow melts' to encourage a discouraged student.

examples.zh: 他在困难时期常念“大雪压青松，青松挺且直；要知松高洁，待到雪化时”。
examples.en: In hard times he often recited 'heavy snow presses the pine, which stands tall and straight; to know its nobility, wait until the snow melts'.

story.en: Chen Yi's poem 'Green Pine' is one of his best-known short poems and is widely taught.
story.zh: 《青松》是陈毅最知名的短诗之一，广为传诵。

usage.en: Quoted to praise integrity and endurance in adversity; the pine stands for steadfast character. The poem is often quoted in this combined form.
usage.zh: 用来称赞逆境中的节操和坚韧，青松象征坚贞品格。此诗常以这一合并形式引用。

text: 断头今日意如何？创业艰难百战多
pinyin: duàn tóu jīn rì yì rú hé, chuàng yè jiān nán bǎi zhàn duō
literal: cut · head · today · feeling · how, found · enterprise · hard · hundred · battles · many
natural: facing the executioner today, how do I feel? Founding a cause is hard and the battles have been many

meaning.en: Chen Yi's opening lines from a poem written when surrounded and expecting to die: how does it feel to face execution? The founding of the cause has been hard, with a hundred battles.
meaning.zh: 陈毅在被围困、准备牺牲时所作诗的开头：今天将要杀头，心情如何？创业艰难，身经百战。

equivalents: facing death, undaunted
a hard road and a hundred battles

examples.zh: 纪念馆里陈列着“断头今日意如何？创业艰难百战多”的诗稿。
examples.en: The museum displays the manuscript of 'Facing the executioner today, how do I feel? Founding a cause is hard and the battles many'.

examples.zh: 他读到“断头今日意如何？创业艰难百战多”，不由肃然起敬。
examples.en: Reading 'Facing the executioner today, how do I feel? Founding a cause is hard and the battles many', he was filled with respect.

story.en: Chen Yi wrote the three poems 'Meiling' in 1936 while hiding in the Meiling mountains after the Red Army's departure from Jiangxi, expecting to be captured.
story.zh: 1936年，红军主力撤离后，陈毅被困江西梅岭，自以为难免一死，作《梅岭三章》。

usage.en: Quoted for courage in the face of death and the hardships of a founding struggle. The poem is the first of three, written in 1936 while Chen Yi was trapped in the Meiling mountains in Jiangxi.
usage.zh: 用来称赞面对死亡的勇气和创业的艰辛。此诗为三首之一，1936年陈毅被困于江西梅岭时所作。

text: 手莫伸，手莫伸，伸手必被捉
pinyin: shǒu mò shēn, shǒu mò shēn, shēn shǒu bì bèi zhuō
literal: hand · don't · reach, hand · don't · reach, reach · hand · surely · be · caught
natural: don't reach out your hand; if you do, you will surely be caught

meaning.en: Chen Yi's warning against taking what is not yours: do not stretch out your hand for illicit gain, for whoever does will be caught.
meaning.zh: 陈毅的警句：不要伸手去拿不该拿的东西，伸手就一定会被抓住。

equivalents: crime does not pay
keep your hands clean

examples.zh: 廉政教育展的第一块展板就是“手莫伸，手莫伸，伸手必被捉”。
examples.en: The first panel of the anti-corruption exhibition read 'don't reach out your hand; if you do, you will surely be caught'.

examples.zh: 他把“手莫伸，手莫伸，伸手必被捉”挂在办公室，时时提醒自己。
examples.en: He hung 'don't reach out your hand; if you do, you will surely be caught' in his office as a constant reminder.

story.en: Chen Yi wrote the short poem 'Don't Reach Out Your Hand' as a warning against corruption.
story.zh: 陈毅作《七古·手莫伸》，用以告诫干部不可贪污腐败。

usage.en: Mainly cited in integrity and anti-corruption education. The poem continues 党与人民在监督，万目睽睽难逃脱.
usage.zh: 主要用于廉政教育和反腐宣传。全诗接着写“党与人民在监督，万目睽睽难逃脱”。

text: 老夫喜作黄昏颂，满目青山夕照明
pinyin: lǎo fū xǐ zuò huáng hūn sòng, mǎn mù qīng shān xī zhào míng
literal: old · man · glad · write · dusk · ode, full · eye · green · hills · setting · sun · bright
natural: this old man gladly writes an ode to dusk, with green hills and the evening sun bright in every view

meaning.en: Ye Jianying's verse on growing old with a clear heart: he happily sings the praises of the evening of life, for the hills are green and the setting sun shines bright.
meaning.zh: 叶剑英的诗句：老人乐于歌颂人生的黄昏，因为满眼青山，夕阳一片光明。

equivalents: a bright and happy old age
the evening of life is glorious

examples.zh: 退休后，他写下“老夫喜作黄昏颂，满目青山夕照明”自勉。
examples.en: After retirement he wrote 'this old man gladly writes an ode to dusk, with green hills and bright evening sun' to encourage himself.

examples.zh: 老年大学的毕业册上印着“老夫喜作黄昏颂，满目青山夕照明”。
examples.en: The senior university's yearbook printed 'this old man gladly writes an ode to dusk, with green hills and bright evening sun'.

story.en: Ye Jianying wrote 'On Turning Eighty' as a reflection on old age.
story.zh: 叶剑英作《八十书怀》，抒发晚年感怀。

usage.en: Quoted for an optimistic, vigorous attitude to old age. It is the closing couplet of the poem.
usage.zh: 用来表达对晚年积极乐观的态度。此联是该诗的尾联。
